Group all major updates into one monthly PR
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Security patches get immediate PRs, auto-merge
nusb is the entire USB layer and a 0.x crate, so its minor bumps are breaking and can change device behavior in ways only real hardware shows. Never auto-merge it.

windows is the WPD backend's whole COM layer and a 0.x crate. CI builds it on Windows but has no device to run it against. Never auto-merge it. Bump windows-core to the same version in the same PR (see docs/dependency-updates.md).

windows-core must stay on exactly the version windows pulls in: it's a direct dependency only so the #[implement] macro's paths resolve. Bumped alone, it can't compile. It moves by hand together with windows.
serial_test 4 needs Rust 1.93.1, and CI runs our tests on the 1.85 MSRV. Lift this hold when the MSRV reaches 1.93.1.

CI runs Rust at the MSRV (rust-version in Cargo.toml) and at stable. A bumped toolchain literal silently stops CI from checking the MSRV, so the toolchain only moves with a deliberate MSRV raise (see docs/dependency-updates.md).
The libmtp comparison benchmark is a manual dev tool outside default-members, built only with libmtp installed locally. CI never compiles it, so a bump here can't be verified.
